summary: The recorded base reproduces the missing direct-abort LoRARegistry release. The exact candidate schedules that release and correctly constrains the existing 500/503 consumer fallback to the exact request state it still owns, preventing double release and reused-RID corruption. Candidate and independent exactly-once boundary tests pass.

tests.what_was_measured: On recorded base 358c163, the candidate's original-issue regression failed because LoRARegistry.release was awaited zero times after direct abort.
At exact candidate commit 1216431, four focused release-accounting and non-LoRA boundary tests passed.
At the exact candidate, the complete RID cleanup module passed: 30 tests and 3 subtests.
Two independently authored cases passed: duplicate abort releases exactly once, and an old error consumer cannot release or delete a newly reused RID state.
The exact candidate diff has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution_evidence: The assigned AMD Instinct MI355X was visible as gfx950, but no GPU execution is claimed: the issue and changed code are CPU-side Python async LoRARegistry accounting, so GPU numerical output would be unrelated proof.
remaining_limitations: No live serving run with real model weights and a real LoRA adapter was performed.
No model architecture, semantic accuracy, adapter-eviction throughput, or distributed-workload claim is made.
The candidate changes no native code, so no native rebuild was applicable.
